clue.text: This puts primate in bad shape

definitions.text: This puts primate in bad shape

indicators.note: puts, read with the later in, means one thing is placed inside another
in, paired with the earlier puts, says where the monkey goes: inside the scrambled word
bad suggests the word is spoilt and its letters jumbled

parts.note: the titi is a small South American monkey, a primate

explanation.surface: A warning about an illness that leaves a monkey in poor condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' signals the anagram and 'puts ... in' the insertion. The titi is an obscure monkey; the whole clue doubles as the definition, since a liver disease would leave one in poor health.
explanation.definitionFit: Hepatitis is inflammation of the liver, an illness that would leave any animal, monkey included, very unwell.

clue.text: Hypnotic state under heaving forces bar

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece under another comes after it
heaving means lifting up, and in a down clue lifting a word makes it read from the bottom up

parts.note: forces as in armed forces means men
bar as a preposition means except, as does but
AL is the abbreviation for the US state of Alabama

explanation.surface: Someone in a trance-like state beneath a mass of military personnel pushing against a barrier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heaving' turns MEN upward to NEM; in this down clue, 'under' puts AL (Alabama) below the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Nembutal is the trade name of a barbiturate sedative, a sleep-inducing drug, which is what a hypnotic is as a noun.

clue.text: Queen of the Netherlands thrashed farceur

parts.note: thrashed means beat, defeated soundly
Brian Rix was a British actor famous for staging and starring in stage farces

explanation.surface: A Dutch monarch giving a comic actor a beating.
explanation.walkthrough: Brian RIX was the leading British farce actor-manager of the postwar decades.
explanation.definitionFit: Beatrix reigned as monarch of the Netherlands from 1980 to 2013.

clue.text: Lesser attraction who is unfortunately plugged by O'Connor

indicators.note: plugged by means having something stuffed into its middle, so one piece goes inside the other
unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: Des O'Connor was a British singer and TV entertainer

explanation.surface: Asking which minor act got blocked by a famous entertainer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges WHO IS. Des O'Connor was a long-running British TV host and crooner.
explanation.definitionFit: A sideshow is a minor show or stall at a fair, secondary to the main event.

clue.text: Perhaps Higgins was a wizard

definitions.meaning: Alex Higgins was a famous snooker player, and someone who sinks balls in snooker is called this
Harry of that surname is the boy wizard of the J K Rowling books

explanation.surface: A remark that a certain Higgins had magical powers.
explanation.walkthrough: Alex Higgins was a Northern Irish snooker champion; 'was' is a link between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A snooker player sinks or pots balls, and Harry of the same surname is a fictional schoolboy sorcerer.

clue.text: Company producing hot running water

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
the Ouse is a river in England, a body of running water

explanation.surface: A firm that supplies hot water from the tap.
explanation.walkthrough: The OUSE is one of several English rivers of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: A house is a business firm, as in a publishing or fashion house.

clue.text: Safe card play

definitions.meaning: in criminal slang a ... is a strongbox that a safe-cracker blows
in bridge and whist, playing a high card then a low one in a suit to signal is called a ...

explanation.definitionFit: Old underworld slang names a strongbox this, and bridge players use the same word for a high-low signalling play.

clue.text: Here it is; accommodation ready for Costa Rican

parts.note: a semi is a semi-detached house, a form of accommodation
ready means cash, and the colon is the currency of Costa Rica

explanation.surface: A housing advert pointing out a home available to someone from Costa Rica.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points at the punctuation mark printed right after 'is'. 'Ready' is British slang for cash; a SEMI is a house sharing one wall with its neighbour.
explanation.definitionFit: The punctuation mark the clue itself prints after the third word is this mark, a dot over a comma.

clue.text: Engine oil?

definitions.meaning: the ... engine is the four-stroke internal combustion engine named after Nikolaus ...
a variant of attar, the fragrant oil from rose petals

explanation.definitionFit: Nikolaus Otto gave his name to the four-stroke engine cycle, and attar of roses, a perfume oil, is also called otto.

clue.text: He doesn't score many runs, getting bowled within a short time

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: within means the piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a bit is a short while, as in wait a bit
B is the cricket abbreviation for bowled

explanation.surface: A cricket report on a poor batsman soon dismissed.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one sentence about a batsman, but the definition stops at 'many'; 'runs' supplies R. In cricket a rabbit is a hopeless batter.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket slang a rabbit is a feeble batsman, usually a tail-ender who rarely makes a decent score.

clue.text: Profound work from a setter I found amazing

indicators.note: amazing here suggests the letters are thrown into astonishing disorder

explanation.surface: A reader praising a deep book by a crossword setter they admire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amazing' rearranges A SETTER I; 'found' and 'from' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A treatise is a lengthy formal written study of a subject, a weighty piece of writing.

clue.text: 'Six and out, sir!' sadly does for players like KP?

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals

indicators.note: sadly suggests the words are upset, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cricketer hits a six and is then given out, lamented by commentators.
explanation.walkthrough: KP is Kevin Pietersen, a flamboyant England batsman. 'sadly' rearranges OUT SIR to RTUOSI.
explanation.definitionFit: Virtuosi are performers of outstanding skill, and a dazzling batsman is such a player.

clue.text: Seen in March, a really fast runner

indicators.note: seen in means the letters can be spotted inside the following words

explanation.surface: A naturalist reports spotting a very speedy animal in the spring.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls the mad March hare.
explanation.definitionFit: The animal is famously swift, able to outpace most predators across open fields.

clue.text: Encompassing specs, shore up rickety old institutional dwelling

indicators.note: encompassing means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other
rickety means unsteady, falling apart, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: specs are spectacles, pictured as two round lenses, OO

explanation.surface: Propping up a tumbledown old building while wearing glasses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rickety' rearranges SHORE UP and 'Encompassing' wraps it round OO, a picture of a pair of glasses.
explanation.definitionFit: A poorhouse was a historic public establishment where paupers were housed and set to work.

clue.text: Sick president finally boarding flight for summit

indicators.note: boarding means getting on, so the pieces go inside the other one

parts.note: a hop is a short flight
sick means ill

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: An unwell head of state gets on a plane to attend a summit meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Summit' looks like a political meeting, but it means a peak.
explanation.definitionFit: The top of a hill is the highest point or summit.

clue.text: Chopped up one alder tree

indicators.note: chopped up suggests cutting the words into bits and reassembling them

explanation.surface: A forester felling one alder tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The oleander is an evergreen flowering shrub or small tree of the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Consume small flounder

parts.note: to flounder is to wallow, struggle clumsily in mud or water

explanation.surface: An instruction to eat a little flatfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flounder' looks like the fish but is the verb meaning to struggle.
explanation.definitionFit: To swallow food is to eat it down, so it is a synonym of consume.

clue.text: Leading light left university pregnant with virtuous mother coming round

indicators.note: coming round means surrounding, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: the Virgin Mary is the virtuous mother of Jesus
in means pregnant, as in an animal said to be in calf or in foal

explanation.surface: A prominent figure quits college, expecting a child, with a good mother visiting.
explanation.walkthrough: IN for pregnant comes from farm usage such as a cow being in calf; 'coming round' has the Virgin's name wrap it.
explanation.definitionFit: A luminary is an eminent person who inspires others, a figure of note.

clue.text: Player contains Lyle, leaving Sandy ultimately in a bit of a hole

indicators.note: contains means one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: Gary Player is a famous South African golfer

indicators.note: leaving means one letter departs from the name

parts.note: Sandy Lyle is a Scottish golfer

indicators.note: ultimately picks the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A golf story: one golfer beating another who lands in a bunker.
explanation.walkthrough: Gary Player and Sandy Lyle are both golf champions; 'leaving' drops Y (the last letter of Sandy) from LYLE to give LLE.
explanation.definitionFit: In mining, a gallery is a horizontal passage, one part of an underground working.

clue.text: Shed fat bulges at intervals getting fit

indicators.note: shed means discard, so letters are thrown away
at intervals means taking every other letter

explanation.surface: Losing weight from flabby bits by regular exercise to get in shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shed' and 'at intervals' together drop every other letter of FAT BULGES, keeping the second, fourth, sixth and eighth.
explanation.definitionFit: Fit in the sense of capable or competent, as in fit for duty.

clue.text: Card game could be pontoon

definitions.meaning: a card game for four players in partnerships
a pontoon is a floating structure supporting a crossing over water

explanation.definitionFit: The partnership card game shares its name with a structure spanning a river, and a pontoon is one kind.

clue.text: Palace almah's exotic underwear

indicators.note: exotic suggests something strange and foreign, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: an almah is an Egyptian dancing girl; the possessive adds no letter
a bra is an item of underwear

explanation.surface: An Egyptian dancer's foreign lingerie.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alhambra is the Moorish palace and fortress complex at Granada in Spain.

clue.text: Fell from height causing pain

parts.note: an ill is a hurt or trouble

explanation.surface: Someone toppled from a great height, causing injury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fell' looks like the past tense of fall, but it is the noun used in northern England for a hill or moor.
explanation.definitionFit: A fell is a high upland or mountain in the north of England.

clue.text: Dead keen to become a painter

parts.note: keen means avid, enthusiastic

explanation.surface: Someone desperately eager to become an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: Jacques-Louis David was a French neoclassical painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacques-Louis David was a celebrated French artist of the Napoleonic era.

clue.text: Indian newspaper?

definitions.meaning: an Indian citizen is one example of a person belonging to a nation
a paper sold across the whole country, as opposed to a local or regional one

explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of India is an example of a person of a given nationality, and the UK's countrywide daily papers carry the same collective name.

clue.text: Capital initially lying close by a river

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word

parts.note: on can mean next to, as in a town on the coast
the Don is a river in Russia and also in England

explanation.surface: A city that lies near a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is literally true: the city lies on the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: London is the capital city of the United Kingdom.

clue.text: One sovereign's no good for a plant

indicators.note: no means without, so the following word is taken away

parts.note: Good King Henry is a leafy plant related to spinach
taken as written

explanation.surface: A king who is a bad lot, compared to a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: Good King Henry is a wild herb of the goosefoot family; take away GOOD and a monarch is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Any of England's eight monarchs of that name was a single ruler.

clue.text: Confidence in football stars ultimately keeping dry? Just the opposite

indicators.note: keeping means holding something inside
just the opposite means the container and contents swap roles from how the surface reads them

parts.note: TT means teetotal, so dry, not drinking alcohol
RU stands for Rugby Union, a form of football

indicators.note: ultimately picks the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Faith in football players managing to stay off the drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface has the stars keeping dry; 'Just the opposite' flips it so the dry piece does the keeping. Football here is rugby, the oval-ball game.
explanation.definitionFit: Trust is faith or belief in someone, so it means much the same as confidence.
